title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
statement: Each row is sorted ascending and each column is sorted ascending. Return the kth smallest value in the whole matrix, counting duplicates separately rather than as one value.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 300, the matrix is n by n
rows and columns are each sorted ascending
duplicates count individually, so the 2nd smallest of [1,1] is 1
hints: Flattening and sorting is O(n^2 log n) and throws away the ordering you were given. Use it.
Merge the n sorted rows with a min-heap seeded by the first element of each row; pop k times, pushing the next element of whichever row you popped from.

There is a better one: binary search on the ANSWER VALUE rather than on a position. For a candidate value, count how many entries are less than or equal to it by walking the staircase from the bottom-left in O(n). That gives O(n log(range)) and no heap at all.
complexity: O(k log n) with a heap, O(n log(range)) with binary search
